0.texto: The Fool is on his way in his bright court-jester's clothes and is about to take the fatal step that will send him over a cliff, lost as he is in his own fancy. Whatever the reasons that have driven him to seek out and circle his nadir, the fool stands for the person who is beginning to commit themselves to a path of personal development; they have come into contact with the soul (or the body) of a living tradition and are in the process of being admitted or initiated into it. Happy to be starting, they have no clear awareness of what awaits them. The cliff at their feet is the abyss of the unknown. And the great unknown here is themselves. The leap into the abyss is the decided movement of introversion from the heights of the conscious ego personality down into the unknown depths of the subconscious — and from the world of sensation and of effects to the dark world of causes and archetypes. A dog, standing for their feeling of dissatisfaction and their small awareness, helps them take the step. The colourless flower in their hand is the emptiness of their fascination, and the bundle on their back holds the baggage of small ambitions they have no intention of giving up for now.

1.texto: With the first instruction, the one who begins to climb the path Malkuth – Yesod becomes the Magician: a young figure, dressed in the robes of the office, standing before a table on which the four elemental magical weapons are laid out. One raised hand holds a double-pointed wand, while the left hand points at the ground as though setting out the principle of analogy («As above, so below») and of channelling. What stands out is how extraordinarily young this figure is: it shows that the subject of the story is beginning to learn. Before them are the instruments — the basic potential — and they even know some principles and laws, but their knowledge is fundamentally theoretical and they do not yet know how to use them. They are surrounded by flowers to show the immense glamour of their state: they believe it is all a matter of information and technique, that with certain exercises they will reach supreme enlightenment. Their mind, however, is open to every influence and that is why they can learn very fast. Their virgin state holds infinite potential and they carry that symbol above their head.

2.texto: Eventually the learner reaches the gates of Yesod and there comes face to face with the High Priestess. She appears seated before the two pillars of manifestation, in front of a veil on which the Tree of Life is drawn. She has power, as the two horns of her crown that touch Chokmah and Binah show; and her power is specifically Daath — Knowledge, the sefirah that forms the core of this crown. In her hands she holds a scroll of the Torah, the Law, of which she is the interpreter, although we see only her left arm, the receptive and not the active aspect; and in the folds of her dress hangs a lunar crescent that points to the immense activity of the ebb and flow of the etheric currents and tides. In these folds are lost those who try to force their way through: astray and deluded in a world of mirages, they glamorise as they please and claim to have cosmic consciousness. The Priestess is Yesod seen from Malkuth: the critical point where all the emanations of the Tree of Life are received and channelled. The veil keeps us from understanding how the law really works — only the effects are perceived, not the causes; we call the law of karma chance because we do not understand how thoughts, feelings and actions are the cause of effects in an endless chain. To go further and lift a corner of the veil, trust is needed, without falling either into the scepticism that blocks psychism or into the credulity that leaves you defenceless before the magnetism of this great glamouriser. A will to serve is needed too, since the Priestess is all dedication and wants nothing for herself.

3.texto: If you manage to get past the High Priestess successfully, you begin to climb the path Yesod – Hod, which is the path of the Empress, the goddess of fertility crowned with stars, the goddess of form and of the universal mind. The Empress is pregnant, but on the plane of ideas: the one moving forward is at the level of studying the mechanism of Cosmic Law, and their mind is fertile ground in which the seeds of the doctrine bear fruit, symbolised by the countless ears of wheat in front of the figure. Meanwhile, and as if to allow all the new knowledge to be taken in, the emotions enter a new holding pattern and do not press too hard — a situation symbolised by the wood and the green water of Netzach falling merrily in a cascade, and by the pale green sign of Venus on the heart on which the Empress sits.

4.texto: It is in the nature of thought to separate, analyse, typify, classify, label. The intellect feeds on facts, explanations and theories, and does not concern itself with their value for life or their ethical value. The Emperor shows the one moving forward stuffed with theory: they have studied all the information the system can give them, they know the mechanics of things and have an explanation and a remedy for everything; they believe they know it all and hold the truth. They also have a certain simple practice, but they have barely touched the pillar of force yet and have not worked much on themselves. The card shows the negative extreme that can be reached: the ego fortified and asserting itself on the throne of its conceptions of the world, a grey stone seat in front of steep mountains — the heights of thought. Everything breathes rigidity, aridity and sterility; only a small stream runs, hemmed in, because emotion cannot be suppressed altogether, though it can be confined. It is a normal state of development, fortunately a passing one, though there are those who anchor themselves in it. Paradoxically the solution is to study more and more deeply: first, to get past the arrogance of believing you know everything; second, because a firm base of knowledge is needed; third, to force the mind to recover its natural balance. The next swing of the pendulum leads to the pillar of force.

5.texto: From Hod you enjoy a little perspective and you look back to see where you have come from, what you have achieved and what what you have learnt has to do with the world: this looking at Malkuth from Hod is the card of the Hierophant. The one moving forward, in their theoretical self-sufficiency, not only believes they know, but feels driven to preach to others; they are also sectarian, because holding the truth implies that others do not hold it. It is a normal stage of development: there is an inflation of the ego, not only because of the fictitious clarity of the ideas, but because belonging to a school has given a sense of identity and importance. The world is seen in terms of masters and disciples, and other people's degree of initiation is measured. What the group's great figures of reference say is taken almost as the word of God; you preach with the authority of the masters and the doctrine, not with your own — an authority that flows naturally only when it turns into living knowledge. The best attitude in these circumstances is to teach formally: that is why, in development groups, those who have already had a strong contact with Hod are asked to start teaching the beginners.

6.texto: This card is a version of the myth of Adam and Eve: our first parents stand naked, each in front of a tree that symbolises their specific nature — the fire of the mind and the rational nature on one side, the emotional nature and the sensuality of the instincts on the other. One looks at the other, enraptured, while the other raises their eyes towards the great solar angel whose presence can be made out behind clouds. It is the card of the passage from Hod to Netzach, while the purple mountain of Yesod appears in the far background. The one moving forward feels magnetised by their emotional side and does not yet sense the presence of the self symbolised by the angel. What can happen at this stage is that they begin to feel strong tugs from the pillar of force: the emotional nature presses hard to leave the relative clarity of the world of abstractions, tides start to be felt rising from the unconscious and partly struggling for possession of the mind. As a result, you lose yourself in your emotions — you may fall in love in the literal sense of the word — but this shifting step is a first meeting with yourself again, though not yet directly.

7.sendero: Condition of the initiate of Netzach
7.texto: The card tells us about the condition of the initiate of Netzach: a showily dressed figure, in a chariot made of heavy grey stone with which their legs merge — inseparable from the chariot — in the attitude of steering it, but with no reins. Its motive power consists of two sphinxes sitting calmly on the grass, with animal bodies and human faces: they symbolise the instinctive and emotional natures, one white and one black, showing the dual principle of their operation — positive and negative, pleasure and pain, good and bad. The meaning of the card is clear: the emotions have been found, but on their own they lead nowhere — you do not yet know how to steer them — without that causing much dismay, busy as you are satisfying the narcissism of the ego. On the inner ground there is already some practice in the relevant techniques, some power over the elements, an ability to build and carry out rituals — but nothing creative is done with it. You are ready for everything, but you do nothing.

8.texto: From your position in Netzach, with the newly won perspective on your own emotions, you look back again: this activity is the card of Justice, the judgement of the emotions upon the world. You are now fully immersed in the illusion of Netzach: projection. You see the speck in someone else's eye, but not the plank in your own; the ideas are clear and sharp, and are used like a sword to dissect other people. You are supposed to know everything about them and their motives; life seems unfair towards your own needs, and you do not understand why things are not as you would want them. In short, objective judgement is darkened by your own projections. Behind is the veil of Yesod, symbolised by the heavy purple curtain between the pillars of the card.

9.texto: The card shows an old figure, eyes closed and hooded, gathered inwards. He holds up a lantern in which a six-pointed star shines, a symbol of the doctrine, and feels his way with a long staff, a symbol of his own assessments. The Hermit is the card of the path Netzach – Yesod: it represents a return to oneself, a decided movement of introversion in search of the truth of oneself and of life. He is old because he is already old in the experiences of the sefirot of the lower face of the Tree of Life; as a result of the conflict between one's own emotional nature and the outside world that Justice pointed to, he has decided that he has had enough of trying to get along with others — and of trying to explain himself or convince them! — and now he is going to devote himself to himself. He has to reconcile his discordant experiences with the doctrine he follows. What he is fleeing from, however, is his own shadow: the result is a movement of withdrawal and introspection.

10.texto: The Wheel of Fortune is Yesod behind the veil. The learning and your own sight of the machinery of the universe have taught you the reality that everything is cyclical, that everything is linked and balanced: every cause has an effect that is the cause of another effect, back to the first cause. Up to a point you are already able to control your own balance; placed on the path Yesod – Tiphereth, the Wheel is receptive to the direct influences of that last sefirah. So it is a relative point of arrival, which brings on a certain stillness and self-satisfaction at the state reached: you believe you know, that you understand. The growing sensitivity to inner states makes you believe you are in contact with the Cosmic Powers, falling into a more sophisticated form of glamour than the Magician's — no longer the fascination with occultism as a whole, but the glamour of the Inner Planes, with their guides, masters and angelic contacts — while you are still immersed in the wheel of your own archetypes. What is your own and is not taken on as such appears projected as someone else's; there are situations and problems that keep coming back and to which, however hard you try, you are unable to give a final answer. But every revolution of the Wheel, every cycle of experience through the lower face of the personality, brings you one point closer to Tiphereth: on each turn the door of Tiphereth opens for a while. If you manage to break with your own security and dare to cross it, the mystery of your own life is resolved; if you turn back, another full cycle awaits until the chance comes round again.

11.texto: Strength is the card of awakening, in this case a gentle awakening by the direct path Yesod – Tiphereth. It portrays a figure, to symbolise that this is not an act of brute force, closing with a soft and graceful gesture the jaws of a lion — the king of the animal kingdom — showing that the roaring voice of the ego has found a point of rest. It all happens over the green fields of Netzach, a sign that victory over one's own emotions has at last been won: it is experiencing a change of gear up the middle pillar. Without violence or effort, as though by an act of grace, the voice of the ego has fallen silent and you enter the luminous world of the self and of being. The flowers that filled the Magician's garden are now the adornment of your own robes, showing that the self radiates beauty; once again there is infinite potential above the head. The self has been found — the question now is what to do with it. The apparent ease of this passage, which happens from above, does not mean that the self is won for ever: it also has to be consolidated by the paths Netzach – Tiphereth (Death) and Hod – Tiphereth (the Hanged Man), or it will be lost.

12.texto: A young figure hangs head down from a beam by one foot, though he seems more suspended than subject to the law of gravity, and gives no feeling of suffering at all; a halo of light surrounds his head. A change of gear from Hod can be experienced like this: after a period of confusion, longer or shorter, your own mental world begins to lose consistency. You begin to know nothing, to understand nothing, and there can be moments of mental emptiness and loss of memory; everything seems futile, unimportant — but one single thing emerges clearly from this chaos, and that thing is yourself. The confusion is followed by periods of great mental clarity: ideas about life and the universe can change radically, and many of the new values are exactly the opposite of the old ones. You stop being self-centred, but you are one step away from pride — this state can bring with it a sterile narcissism or self-contemplation. The cure is to swallow your vanity and get to work on the new path.

13.texto: The experience of this card is dying: dying to the old habits, to the dependencies, to the feelings, to everything that had been put in front of the self. It is the old personality that dies, but since you are that old personality until you are the new one, it turns out that you are the one who dies. Because of the attachments, nothing spares you the pain, the anguish, the desolation and the possible depression of this step; a change of gear from Netzach really hurts. You can lose social position, fame, money, health, family, friends — and the person does not choose: death comes as if from outside, and it is always dramatic. There is a struggle, a resistance to dying, a battle between the ego and the self; when it is experienced from Tiphereth and you already hold a budding tiphrethic consciousness, you notice that you have changed radically and that the things you were tied to are dead. It is a difficult moment, because now the decision is entirely your own. The allegory is clear: it is the relentless passing of death, like a breath that does not stop — and behind its gates, on the far horizon, the sun of tiphrethic consciousness is already rising.

14.texto: The self simply is, and that is what the angel of Temperance does, still half asleep in its new absorption: waiting and being. Now you see clearly who you are, what you want and how to get it; even so, although you could, you do not throw yourself hastily into any action that would compromise the newborn self, still weak and babbling — you limit yourself to being happy in the delight of self-discovery. The whole card breathes an air of gentle balance: the figure is gracefully suspended, one foot on the earth and the other in the water, showing a mid-point between consciousness and subconsciousness. For the moment you are busy rather with consolidating the state, putting a final distance between the self and the ego, tempering the new emotions — symbolised by the water passing from one cup to the other — and getting to grips with the new circumstances of life the change of gear has brought. So, little by little, you climb the path Tiphereth – Geburah, where the next experience is waiting.

15.texto: The card shows a couple chained to the Devil's pedestal, though the loop of chain that binds them by the neck is loose enough to let them free themselves if they wished — a sign that it is their own decision, or that they are unaware of their real situation. The Devil is the power of the will, which can now work freely and unconditioned; a will that can be cold, calculating, able to cut itself off from and ignore any feeling of compassion. Before the change of gear there was the brake of the old foundation, an ethic of broad consensus; now the essential point of reference is yourself, and individuation has released a great deal of energy, making the person a powerful being. You have received a real baptism of fire: the fire that lights, gives life and burns in a flame of pure creative being; the transmuting fire of compassion; and the burning fire of self-fulfilment, of self-love and of pride. If everything you know is used only for yourself, if your own will is law without regard for the means of reaching the ends, if you give in to the illusion of invincibility, the fire becomes an inner burning that burns coldly and slowly, and everywhere you will look to put out that fire that is never satisfied.

16.sendero: Fall down the pillar of form
16.texto: The Tower is the result of having given in to the Devil: a lightning bolt from heaven strikes the tower of the self and you are stripped of the crown of tiphrethic consciousness. As a result you fall down the path Geburah – Hod and, from there, on to Yesod, back to the Wheel of Fortune to start again — this time, however, the process of ascent will be more painful, since the memory of what was achieved and lost will torment you constantly, and it will be harder to open up because the spontaneity and innocence of the first attempt are no longer there. The Tower symbolises a fall down the pillar of form: it can be dramatic, with a sharp conflict outside, inside or both, or it can be gentler, and you find yourself, without knowing how or why, back in Hod, using a language that has lost its vitality and inner strength. The Tower takes place when a level of energy and pressure has been reached that can no longer be controlled: that is why the form breaks. This applies to groups too, and it is more common than you might think.

17.texto: The Star is the cure for everything above; its spirit is that of devotion to the Great Work. Until now you have been concerned fundamentally with your own development; now you begin to develop others. The water is no longer passed continually from one cup to the other, as in Temperance, but poured outwards by the handful: you begin to learn humility, you are truthful with yourself and with others, without falsification or pretension. As a whole person you fulfil the triad of Chesed / Geburah / Tiphereth, and the influence is positive and constructive — you cannot reach this state without a real concern for others, and it is necessary to open up, naked and vulnerable, trusting. The Star is the star of Kether and of hope, surrounded by seven other stars that are the logoi of the seven planes; the field of action is that of the elements and of the ethers, over which influence is also poured. In the distance, a bird symbolises the inner vehicles that wait for the work to be completed in order to make the flight of consciousness across the abyss.

18.texto: In Chesed you find the card of the Moon: the Moon is the self in meditation, a calm and deeply concentrated face drawn on the lunar disc. The Moon looks inwards: in its fullness and roundness, sharply marked out against the darkness of the primordial night sky, it puts you in touch with the deep levels of the primitive psyche. Here you come into contact with the archetypes of the collective unconscious, you look at your deepest fears and you trace the path of your own reincarnations. The unconscious becomes progressively conscious; there is nothing fascinating in this and there is no room left for glamour — you face reality, you see everything that has made you what you are. In the card, a sea creature coming out of the water begins the upward path of life that disappears on the far horizon of the mountains; on either side, a dog and a wolf — the tamed nature and the wild one — look at the moon, as your own animal nature waits to be enlightened and redeemed. Beyond, two twin towers symbolise the next stage of evolution, this time human and cultural, but they are also the gates of Hades beyond the river of no return.

19.texto: If you have preferred imagination to reality, giving in to glamour; if you have refused to face what you are and why; if you have yielded to the illusion of Chesed or to the temptation of martyrdom, then you fall down the path Chesed – Netzach, much more gently and sweetly than by the path of the Tower, but, as then, to start again from the Wheel. The love of Chesed has turned into the sentimentality of Netzach: you deflate into an idealism as sterile as it is utopian, and you shed tears of self-pity and of not being understood by others. And before you know it, you are separated from the sun by a thick brick wall, leaving the garden of sunflowers behind, while the king of stars says goodbye with a slightly frowning gesture: you have enjoyed the glamour of pomp and show, both of them vices of Chesed, and you have preferred to go on being a child crowned with flowers and feathers, carrying a monumental banner.

20.sendero: Looking again at Tiphereth from Chesed
20.texto: If, on the contrary, you have got past the moon satisfactorily, from the position of Chesed you look again at Tiphereth, and this experience is the card of Judgement. The great angel of the self sounds the trumpet and the dead who are the past lives rise from the sea of the unconscious; the judgement now is on yourself and it is an objective judgement, unlike the case of Justice. You understand your own law of karma and you work on it actively; with the final redemption of your own nature, the self is complete. You have reached total freedom and the power to decide over your own life and your own death.

21.texto: You know your own self at every level and you are a fully realised individual; you are one, in Daath, with the manifestations of the Holy Living Creatures, which now appear in the foreground and in full colour — although only their heads, to show that they are not really four separate beings. With every illusion transcended, you dance the dance of form and you wear the purple veil of manifestation: consciousness and action are one, and that is why symbols of the two pillars appear in the hand, now both white, to show pure mercy. You have reached the end and everything begins again, though at another level — that is why in Daath you have the card of the Fool again: once more with your things over your shoulder, something urges you to go on and cross the Abyss, to decide to knock again at the door of the Eternal Unknown.
